about: Zenkai Rules Z1 intent examples: card t_90e75c20, per-case disk retention. gauntlet.store.RunDir.retain(case_id, keep) deletes everything under that case's workdir except files matching a `keep` glob pattern, and reports bytes freed; an empty keep tuple (bulk's own policy: score-only) empties the whole workdir; a case with no workdir is a no-op. Run by tests/intent/test_case_retention_intent.py directly against gauntlet.store.RunDir -- no darktable, no real gauntlet run. Two oracles per example: whether the kept file still exists afterward, and the exact byte count freed -- a retention pass that frees the right number of bytes but deletes the wrong file (or vice versa) is as wrong as one that does nothing.
subject: gauntlet/store.py:RunDir.retain

examples.source: card t_90e75c20: keep only the sidecar/XMP, delete imported originals/copies
bulk (import_and_cull) = score-only: nothing survives after the verdict is written
a case whose session never staged anything must never error or fabricate bytes freed
